# Test fixtures

A fake but internally-consistent Zotero library, for tests that need to
exercise `zotero_sync.local_api`, `zotero_sync.bbt_client`, `zotero_sync.
annotations`, and `zotero_sync.sync` without a real running Zotero. This
directory ships fixtures/stubs only — no pytest test cases live here (see
issues #5 and #6, which consume these).

## What's here

- `zotero.sqlite` — a real sqlite3 database (generated by
  `build_zotero_sqlite.py`, checked in as binary) containing the minimal
  `items` / `itemAttachments` / `itemAnnotations` tables/columns that
  `annotations.py` reads. 3 paper items, one PDF attachment each, and 4
  annotations on two of them: 2 highlights + 1 non-highlight (type=2, e.g.
  a sticky note) on the first paper, 1 highlight on the second, and zero
  annotations on the third. The non-highlight row exists specifically to
  prove `sync.ANNOTATION_TYPE_HIGHLIGHT` filtering works.
- `build_zotero_sqlite.py` — the generator for `zotero.sqlite`. Rerun it
  (`python tests/fixtures/build_zotero_sqlite.py`) to regenerate the file
  after editing the DATA constants in that script. Its module docstring
  documents the schema (which tables/columns exist and why) and the
  itemID/key/citekey mapping table.
- `local_api/items.json` — a static JSON fixture matching what
  `local_api.list_paper_items()` parses (a page from `GET /items` or
  `GET /collections/<key>/items`). 5 entries: 3 bibliographic items across
  different `itemType`s (journalArticle, conferencePaper, bookSection) plus
  one `note` and one `attachment`, so a consumer can confirm
  `NON_PAPER_ITEM_TYPES` filtering. Includes creators (both `name` and
  `firstName`/`lastName` forms), tags (one plain/manual, one `type: 1`
  auto-derived tag), and `collections` membership.
- `local_api/collections.json` — matches `local_api.list_collections()`.
  Two collections: "Research" (top-level, `parentCollection: false`) and
  "Machine Learning" (child of Research), to exercise nested-collection
  parent resolution in `sync._collection_maps()`.
- `bbt/citationkeys.json` — a full Better BibTeX JSON-RPC response envelope
  (`{"jsonrpc", "id", "result"}`) matching what `bbt_client.citationkeys()`
  expects back from `body["result"]`. Maps `"1:<key>"` item ids (library id
  1 = BBT's "My Library", matching `sync.BBT_LIBRARY_ID`) to citekeys for
  the same 3 paper items used in `items.json`.
- `stub_server.py` — `ZoteroStubServer`, a stdlib-only (`http.server`) HTTP
  server that serves the fixtures above on an OS-assigned localhost port,
  routing both Local API paths (`/api/users/0/items`,
  `/api/users/0/collections`, `/api/users/0/collections/<key>/items`) and
  the BBT JSON-RPC endpoint (`/better-bibtex/json-rpc`, handling
  `api.ready` and `item.citationkey`).

Item ids/keys are consistent across all three fixtures and the sqlite file
— see the table in `build_zotero_sqlite.py`'s docstring.

## How a future test wires this up

`local_api.py` and `bbt_client.py` hardcode their target host/port as
module-level constants (`local_api.BASE_URL`, `bbt_client.RPC_URL`) rather
than reading them from `Config`, since in real use they always talk to
Zotero's fixed local port 23119. There's nothing to configure through
`Config` — a test instead monkeypatches those two constants to point at the
stub's actual (OS-assigned) port, and points a copy of `zotero.sqlite` at
wherever the code under test expects the db copy to live:

```python
import shutil
import pytest

from zotero_sync import bbt_client, local_api
from tests.fixtures.stub_server import ZoteroStubServer, FIXTURES_DIR


@pytest.fixture
def zotero_stub(monkeypatch):
    server = ZoteroStubServer()
    server.start()
    monkeypatch.setattr(local_api, "BASE_URL", server.local_api_base_url)
    monkeypatch.setattr(bbt_client, "RPC_URL", server.bbt_rpc_url)
    yield server
    server.stop()


@pytest.fixture
def zotero_sqlite_copy(tmp_path):
    # Mirrors what annotations.copy_database() does against a real
    # install — tests should never open the checked-in fixture directly,
    # since some code paths (schema verification, connection lifecycle)
    # are worth exercising against a throwaway copy.
    dest = tmp_path / "zotero.sqlite"
    shutil.copy2(FIXTURES_DIR / "zotero.sqlite", dest)
    return dest
```

From there:

- Ticket #5 (unit tests) can call `local_api.list_paper_items()`,
  `bbt_client.citationkeys()`, `annotations.item_ids_by_key()`,
  `annotations.read_annotations()`, `sync.build_papers()`, and
  `sync.attach_annotations()` directly against `zotero_stub` /
  `zotero_sqlite_copy`, asserting on the parsed `Paper`/`Annotation`
  dataclasses.
- Ticket #6 (integration test) can instead monkeypatch
  `annotations.default_zotero_sqlite_path()` to return
  `zotero_sqlite_copy`, construct a `Config` pointing at a scratch vault
  directory, and call `sync.run(config)` end-to-end against `zotero_stub`,
  then assert on the Markdown notes written into the vault.

This was verified end-to-end (both fixture composition and the
`sync.build_papers()` → `sync.attach_annotations()` pipeline against the
stub + sqlite together) while building these fixtures; that ad hoc check
was not committed since it isn't a real test (that's #5/#6's job), but
gives confidence the shapes here match what the consuming code actually
expects.
